critique.evidence: The screen directly advances the defense story by translating detection into attacker economics: success falls from 84% to 5%, observed successes from 115 to 7, cost per successful fraud rises from ₹4,721.739 to ₹96,964.286, and attacker ROI falls from 545.35× to 25.60×. It also links the result back to the adaptive arena. However, the claimed campaign-winning framing is not yet supported: post-defense ROI remains 25.60× and is explicitly labeled above break-even, so the attacker is still highly profitable. The screen also provides no visible derivation, time/sample basis, fraud-value assumption, adaptation-cost model, or Mastercard-specific network impact such as prevented loss, authorization impact, false-positive cost, or issuer/acquirer value.
critique.fix: Make the economics demonstrate a defensible win: show inputs and calculation provenance, include adaptation/retooling costs and uncertainty, and present the threshold or trajectory that drives attacker ROI below 0×. Add Mastercard-relevant outcomes—prevented fraud value, affected transaction volume, authorization/false-positive tradeoffs, and issuer/acquirer savings—while clearly distinguishing measured values from modeled projections.
